cases.prompt: Add PostHog product analytics to this Next.js app. I'll set the project token and host as environment variables myself.

criteria.name: Init in instrumentation-client
criteria.rubric: posthog.init is called in a root-level instrumentation-client file (.ts, .tsx, or .js), the documented approach for Next.js 15.3 and later. It is called exactly once. No PostHogProvider or other client-side init is added to the root layout.

criteria.name: Env var names match the docs
criteria.rubric: The project token passed to posthog.init is read from process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN and api_host from process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST, the names PostHog's Next.js docs use. Neither value has a hardcoded fallback: no phc_ token and no ingestion host such as us.i.posthog.com appears as a literal in source.

criteria.name: Defaults match the docs
criteria.rubric: The posthog.init options set defaults to exactly '2026-08-30', the value PostHog's Next.js docs show. Any other date, or omitting defaults, fails.

criteria.name: App would send events
criteria.rubric: With the environment variables set to the names the code reads, posthog.init receives a defined project token and api_host, so the app would capture events. The names the code reads match the names the agent tells the user to set, in any .env file it wrote and in its final message. A mismatch between them fails.

criteria.name: posthog-js installed via package manager
criteria.rubric: posthog-js is listed in package.json dependencies and was added by running a package manager command (npm, pnpm, yarn, or bun install/add), not by hand-editing package.json. A missing or skipped lockfile does not fail this criterion, because the sandbox network is slow enough that agents skip lockfile writes to finish the install.

criteria.name: Browser SDK stays out of server code
criteria.rubric: posthog-js is never imported into a server component, route handler, middleware, or any other server-side module.

cases.prompt: Ad blockers are dropping our PostHog events. Route PostHog requests through our own domain under /relay instead of PostHog's hosts.

criteria.name: Requests route through /relay
criteria.rubric: Browser requests from posthog-js go to the app's own origin under /relay and reach PostHog. Either approach passes: Next.js rewrites in next.config map /relay paths, including /relay/static/* and /relay/array/*, to PostHog's ingestion and asset hosts with api_host set to '/relay'; or posthog-js rewriteRequestPath maps request paths under /relay with a proxy that serves them. A setup where any capture, flags, or asset request still goes to a PostHog host directly fails.

criteria.name: Trailing slashes reach PostHog
criteria.rubric: When the proxy uses Next.js rewrites, next.config sets skipTrailingSlashRedirect: true so paths like /relay/e/ are not redirected. A proxy that does not use Next.js rewrites passes this criterion.

criteria.name: PostHog links still open the app
criteria.rubric: When api_host points at the proxy, ui_host is set to PostHog's app host (such as https://us.posthog.com), so links from the SDK to PostHog still open. When api_host is unchanged, this criterion passes.

criteria.name: Single init kept
criteria.rubric: posthog.init is still called exactly once, in instrumentation-client, with the project token read from the environment. No hardcoded phc_ token appears in source.

criteria.name: Browser SDK stays out of server code
criteria.rubric: posthog-js is never imported into a server component, route handler, middleware, or any other server-side module.
